answer: Trust-graph flow caps: each agent's reward weight comes from random walks started at seed validators and following the thread of real interactions, like paid jobs and co-graded work. A farmer can spin up a thousand fake names, but they touch the honest graph only through the few edges he truly earned, one narrow inlet, so walks rarely reach them and their total weight stays near one honest node's. New edges need audited paid work that peers can cut if it looks staged, so the fakes find no harbor and splitting never adds income.
